newsitem.title: USA: Johnstown Q3 freight car operations off.
newsitem.headline: Johnstown Q3 freight car operations off.

text.p: Johnstown America Industries Inc said on Wednesday that revenues from its freight car operations fell to $53.7 million in the third quarter from $112.5 million a year ago.
The revenue drop reflected a decrease in shipments of new and rebuilt freight cars to 1,084 compared with 2,039 a year earlier.

"Market conditions for our freight car manufacturing business remained severely depressed during the third quarter, which resulted in a sharp decline in revenues compared to last year," Chairman Thomas Begel said in a statement.
He added that the company's freight car rebuilding and repair operation and its freight car leasing subsidiary performed well during the quarter.
Truck components and assemblies operations recorded sales of $56.1 million for the third quarter, down from $68.1 million a year earlier.
Iron foundry operations recorded sales of $30.1 million in the latest quarter, compared with $30.7 million a year earlier.
Earlier, Johnstown America reported a third quarter net loss of $0.16 a share, compared with year-ago earnings of $0.03. Revenues for the quarter dropped to $140.8 million from $166.9 million.
Begel said that the company's financial position and liquidity remain strong.
"Our near-term strategy is to bring costs down even further, manage cash flow and continue to invest in new products and technology that are essential to our future," Begel said.
